cylinders.typicalUse: Recreational single tank (warm water, training, sidemount)
cylinders.notes: Standard rental tank globally; becomes positively buoyant near end of dive. Weight and buoyancy from the Luxfer LAL80 sheet (full -0.80 kg, +1.54 kg at 500 psi, in sea water with valve); empty and at-50-bar are derived from the 500 psi row.

cylinders.typicalUse: Recreational single tank (Asia, some EU regions)
cylinders.notes: Common in Asian dive markets; larger and heavier than AL80.

cylinders.typicalUse: Recreational single tank (smaller divers, shorter dives)
cylinders.notes: Good option between AL63 and AL80; popular for travel and sidemount.
Popular with small-frame divers or kids; lighter but same diameter as AL80. Weight and buoyancy from the Luxfer LAL63 sheet (full -1.1 kg, +0.77 kg at 500 psi, in sea water with valve).

Compact stage/deco bottle; manageable for warm-water tech dives. Weight and full buoyancy from the Luxfer LAL50 sheet (9.7 kg; full -1.13 kg in sea water with valve). Empty and at-50-bar are computed from the weight and water volume (scripts/cylinder-buoyancy.py): the sheet's +0.36 kg at 500 psi sits 1.49 kg above its full row, more than the 1.38 kg of air 6.9 L holds between those pressures, so it cannot be right together with the full row.

Common oxygen bottle for deco; good trim when clipped to left side. Weight and full buoyancy from the Luxfer LAL40 sheet (6.9 kg; full -0.32 kg in sea water with valve). Empty and at-50-bar are computed from the weight and water volume (scripts/cylinder-buoyancy.py): the sheet's +1.13 kg at 500 psi sits 1.45 kg above its full row, more than the 1.14 kg of air 5.7 L holds between those pressures, so it cannot be right together with the full row.
Pony bottle for emergency gas; small enough for travel or boat use. Weight and buoyancy from the Luxfer LAL30 sheet (full -0.68 kg, 0 kg at 500 psi, in sea water with valve).

Very small bailout bottle; close to neutral when empty. Water volume is Luxfer's true LAL19 figure (2.87 L), so its real-gas free gas reads a touch over the marketed 19. Buoyancy from the Luxfer LAL19 sheet (full -0.60 kg, -0.05 kg at 500 psi, in sea water with valve).
Usually mounted for drysuit argon inflation; rarely used for breathing gas. Buoyancy from the Luxfer LAL13 sheet (full -0.80 kg, -0.40 kg at 500 psi, in sea water with valve).
Most common steel tank in Europe; stays negative.
Very dense; allows more gas but heavier topside and affects trim.
Heavy but long bottom time; usually neutral when empty.
Often used as twin 10s for balanced doubles in cold water.
Popular compact steel; often used as twin 10.5s in Europe.
Stage/deco bottle for cold water; remains negative throughout.
Standard 3L rebreather bottle; fits most CCR frames.

Popular cave/wreck tank; slightly positive when empty. Water volume and weight are the Faber LP85 sheet's (13.0 L, 14.2 kg). The sheet lists full -3.80 lb (-1.72 kg) and +2.32 lb (+1.05 kg) at 500 psi. Buoyancy is computed from the weight and water volume (scripts/cylinder-buoyancy.py), in sea water with a valve. Faber's sheet quotes buoyancy without a valve and its row labelled 500 psi is the empty figure (physics without a valve reproduces both rows within 0.17 kg), so the figures here sit about 0.6 kg lower than the sheet.
Cave/wreck doubles workhorse; roughly neutral when empty.

Good trim and buoyancy; favorite single for drysuit divers. Water volume and weight are the Faber FX100 sheet's (12.9 L, 15.6 kg; the sheet's 34.0 lb disagrees with its own kg figure). The sheet lists full -8.41 lb (-3.81 kg) and -0.59 lb (-0.27 kg) at 500 psi. The Worthington/PST X7-100 is a different cylinder (~11.6 L). Buoyancy is computed from the weight and water volume (scripts/cylinder-buoyancy.py), in sea water with a valve. Faber's sheet quotes buoyancy without a valve and its row labelled 500 psi is the empty figure (physics without a valve reproduces both rows within 0.17 kg), so the figures here sit about 0.6 kg lower than the sheet.
Tall and heavy; lots of gas for single-tank tech or long rec dives.

Popular tech diving cylinder; good balance of capacity and trim. Water volume and weight are the Faber FX117 sheet's (15.0 L, 17.7 kg; the sheet's 37.6 lb is 17.05 kg and does not reproduce its own buoyancy rows). The sheet lists full -9.12 lb (-4.14 kg) and +0.35 lb (+0.16 kg) at 500 psi. Buoyancy is computed from the weight and water volume (scripts/cylinder-buoyancy.py), in sea water with a valve. Faber's sheet quotes buoyancy without a valve and its row labelled 500 psi is the empty figure (physics without a valve reproduces both rows within 0.17 kg), so the figures here sit about 0.6 kg lower than the sheet.
Gas monster; heavy and long, often awkward for smaller divers.

Faber's largest single (sometimes called a 130). Heavy, and close to neutral when empty. Water volume and weight are the Faber FX133 sheet's (17.0 L, 19.4 kg). The sheet lists full -9.08 lb (-4.12 kg) and +1.45 lb (+0.66 kg) at 500 psi. Buoyancy is computed from the weight and water volume (scripts/cylinder-buoyancy.py), in sea water with a valve. Faber's sheet quotes buoyancy without a valve and its row labelled 500 psi is the empty figure (physics without a valve reproduces both rows within 0.17 kg), so the figures here sit about 0.6 kg lower than the sheet.
Compact CCR O₂ bottle; easy to travel with and replace.
Standard diluent cylinder for most CCR units; often filled to 232 bar.

cylinders.typicalUse: Longer rec single / big gas in warm water
cylinders.notes: High-capacity aluminum; tall and heavy. Weight and buoyancy from the Luxfer LAL100 sheet (full -2.10 kg, +0.86 kg at 500 psi, in sea water with valve).

Compact steel; stays negative when empty. Water volume and weight are the Faber FX80 sheet's (10.2 L, 13.0 kg). The sheet lists full -8.05 lb (-3.65 kg) and -1.74 lb (-0.79 kg) at 500 psi. Buoyancy is computed from the weight and water volume (scripts/cylinder-buoyancy.py), in sea water with a valve. Faber's sheet quotes buoyancy without a valve and its row labelled 500 psi is the empty figure (physics without a valve reproduces both rows within 0.17 kg), so the figures here sit about 0.6 kg lower than the sheet.
High-capacity HP steel; stays negative.
Popular small LP cylinder in the US; often overfilled in practice.

cylinders.typicalUse: Vintage/ubiquitous US steel; still common on boats
cylinders.notes: Classic 2250 psi steel; slim profile.
Large LP steel; heavy topside; remains negative when empty.

High-capacity LP steel; excellent for long tech dives and doubles. Water volume and weight are the Faber LP108 sheet's (17.0 L, 18.6 kg). The sheet lists full -5.0 lb (-2.27 kg) and +3.0 lb (+1.36 kg) at 500 psi. Buoyancy is computed from the weight and water volume (scripts/cylinder-buoyancy.py), in sea water with a valve. Faber's sheet quotes buoyancy without a valve and its row labelled 500 psi is the empty figure (physics without a valve reproduces both rows within 0.17 kg), so the figures here sit about 0.6 kg lower than the sheet.
Common EU large single; heavy but lots of gas.
Compact EU steel; often used as twin 8.5s.
Very common CCR bottle size; fits many frames.
The EU-standard 232 bar rating of the compact CCR bottle.
The EU-standard 232 bar rating of the common CCR diluent cylinder.
The light 200 bar Faber 12L; popular for sidemount in Europe.
